title: Cross-region fleet prioritization huddle - 2026-03-26
body:
Meeting: Cross-region fleet prioritization huddle
Date: 2026-03-26
Facilitator: Priya Kohli
Note-taker: Miguel Torres
Attendees: Priya, Miguel, Asha, Derrick, Lena, (Ad hoc: Samira from SRE for 20m)
Purpose: Rapid alignment on next-14-day capacity allocation across regions; decide which workloads move to soft reservations vs. burst corridors; identify immediate mitigation for region-specific headwinds.

Key context (brief):
- Usage growth continues for streaming chat workloads; 95th pct per-token compute is up ~12% week-over-week due to larger context windows.
- Two enterprise Dedicated contracts onboarding next month (EU-heavy) which require sustained throughput guarantees.
- Spot capacity in ap-southeast is volatile this week after cloud provider maintenance windows.

Quick dashboard snapshot (as of 2026-03-26 08:00 PDT):
- us-west-2: idle capacity 86 GPUs (A100/80GB equiv), reserved 420, avg latency SLO compliance 99.4% (target 99.5%)
- eu-west-1: idle capacity 18 GPUs (H100-equivalent), reserved 320, rolling deploys causing short pressure windows (see ENGINFRA-4899)
- ap-southeast-1: idle capacity 6 GPUs, reserved 70, spot churn high after provider maintenance; latency SLO 98.1% in burst windows
- overall cross-region spare cushion: ~2.6% of global committed pool (below target 5%)

Observations / region notes:
- us-west-2: healthy but trending down midday; Asha suggests temporary increase in soft-lane reservations for latency-sensitive routes between 12:00–18:00 PDT. Pro: preserves SLO. Con: reduces global burst buffer.
- eu-west-1: several canary jobs caused transient KV cache pressure impacting small-context chat routes. Derrick traced to a rollout (PR #314) that bumped memory footprint. Rollback planned if further incidents.
- ap-southeast-1: provider maintenance created noisy neighbor behavior; short-term option: route lower-priority background embedding jobs to us-west-2 overnight using cheaper burst windows.

Decisions made in meeting:
1) Implement soft-binding reservations (label: soft-resv) for enterprise onboards in eu-west-1 for the first 21 days instead of hard reservations. Purpose: give them predictable throughput without permanently carving capacity. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-28. Linked: ENGINFRA-4821.
2) Create a temporary burst-corridor policy to redirect low-priority batch embeddings from ap-southeast-1 -> us-west-2 during provider maintenance windows (22:00–06:00 local). This will run as a scheduled routing rule for next 10 days. Owner: Miguel. Due: 2026-03-27.
3) Defer non-urgent canary ramp in eu-west-1 until we validate the memory change effects. Derrick will open a short rollback play and a postmortem if another incident observed. Owner: Derrick. Due: immediate/ASAP.

Action items (explicit):
- Priya: Implement soft-resv tagging and update the billing/export mapping so usage appears against reservation buckets. Add alert if soft-resv breach > 10% for 3 consecutive hours. Due 2026-03-28.
- Miguel: Deploy scheduled routing rule (burst-corridor) and smoke-test with synthetic embeddings at 23:00 UTC. Confirm throughput and costs. Due 2026-03-27.
- Asha: Draft a short-runbook for on-call SREs describing how to temporarily expand soft-resv windows for hosted-critical routes. Include thresholds and rollback steps. Due 2026-03-29.
- Derrick: Revert the memory bump patch in PR #314 in eu-west-1 as a canary if we see repeat cache pressure spikes; collect heap/malloc traces when reverting. File incident doc. Due immediate.
- Lena: Run a quick cost delta projection for moving 10% of ap-southeast-1 embeddings to us-west-2 for 10 nights; include cross-region egress estimate. Due 2026-03-27.
- Samira (SRE): Add a short synthetic SLO test that exercises 1k small-context chat flows at 50rps to eu-west-1 canary pool nightly and push results to the capacity dashboard. Due 2026-03-30.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Soft-resv reduces global burst buffer and could make us brittle if multiple regions experience spikes simultaneously. Mitigation: keep two emergency burst lanes unreserved for 72-hour window; automated escalation to capacity ops.
- Risk: Cross-region routing increases egress costs and could add latency for some workflows. Mitigation: limit routing to background/low-priority embeddings and run cost check (Lena).
- Risk: Unobserved memory regression after rollback. Mitigation: enable tracing and short-lived rollout canaries with shorter TTLs.

Open questions / discussion items to carry forward:
- How long should soft-resv remain the default for new enterprise onboards? (options discussed: 21 days / 60 days / until 1 month of traffic baseline) — action: Priya to propose default.
- Should we formalize 'burst corridor' as a first-class scheduling primitive in the scheduler (vs. ad-hoc routing rules)? Miguel to prototype a minimal API next sprint.

Notes to self / shorthand reminders:
- check ENGINFRA-4772 for previous soft-resv experiment results (had good SLO retention but higher cost).
- follow up with Legal on cross-border data routing for embeddings (EU contract nuance).

Next meeting: Mon 2026-03-30 09:00 PDT — quick sync on status of action items + 14-day capacity reforecast.

Appendix: Quick references and snippets
- Temporary routing rule example (pseudo): route if region==ap-southeast-1 and workload.priority==low -> target_region us-west-2 between 22:00-06:00 local. TTL: 10 days.
- Alert thresholds we want (proposal): region_idle_pct < 3% for 2 hours -> pager; soft-resv_breach > 10% for 3h -> page; global_spare_cushion < 2% -> capacity-ops email.

End notes: meeting was intentionally short (40m). Conversation focused on practical, short-lived controls we can apply without long-term architectural changes. People pushed back on long reservation commitments; consensus favored temporary soft-reservation + explicit rollback/metrics.
